osmTags.inscription: The horsa glider of Major R.J. Howard, Oxfordshire And Buckinghamshire Light Infantry, who commanded the operation to capture the bridge landed on this spot together with Lieutenant H.D. Brotheridge and 26 soldiers at 0016 hours on 6 june 1944...

The horsa glider of Lieutenant R.A. Smith, piloted by staff sergeants Barkway and Boyle and also carrying Captain J. Vaughan, Royal Army Medical Corps and 1238 soldiers landed on this spot at 00:18 hours on 6 June 1944...

The horsa glider of lieutenant D.J. Wood, piloted by staff sergeants Boland and Hobbs and also carrying captain H.R.K. Neilson, Royal Engineers and 28 soldiers landed on this spot at 0017 hours on 6 June 1944...
6 VI 1944 L'héroïsme des forces alliées libère les premières les rives de l'Orne|6 VI 1944 The banks of the Orne first parts of France are liberated by the allied forces
To commemorate the action of The 2nd (Airborne) Bn Oxfordshire and Buckinghamshire Light Infantry who captured Pegasus Bridge on the night of 5/6th June 1944...

L'Arbre de la Liberté|En hommage aux hommes de l'opération 'Coup de main' du Major Howard, là où a commencé le Débarquement de Normandie, à Bénouville, dans la nuit du 5 au 6 juin 1944 à 0h16 par la prise du pont devenu Pegasus Bridge...

Major John Howard|Distinguished Service Order|Croix de Guerre avec palme|Company Commander of D Company 2nd Battalion Oxfordshire and Buckinghamshire Light Infantry who were part of 6th Airborne Division...

In front of this house on the 6 June 1944, at 12.02.30 hrs, Commando units landed from the sea, joined forces with elements of 6th Airborne Division dropped from the sky during the night. Two minutes and thirty seconds after the appointed time...
To you of the 6 th Airborne Division|To you of lord Lovat's commando|In memory of 6 th June 1944|We thank you from the bottom of our hearts

This plaque commemorates Lt Col. Rg. Pine-Coffin D.S.O. M.C. Commanding Officer, and 7th Battalion (L.I.) the Parachute Regiment which relieved Major Howard's force at 01:30hrs on 6th June 1944 and held Pegasus Bridge...
Café Gondrée was used as an aid post from the night of 5th June 1944, wherein shelter and medical treatment were given to the casualties of the battle to hold the 6th Airborne Division bridgehead...

This was the first house in France to be liberated during the last hour of 5th June 1944 by men of the Oxfordshire and Buckinghamshire Light Infantry in the British 6th Airborne Division under the command of Major R. John Howard...

Dedicated to the memory of L/Cpl Fred Greenhalgh who was the first Allied serviceman to the on D-Day. A member of the 2nd Battalion The Oxfordshire & Buckinghamshire Light Infantry, he was drowned near this spot having been thrown from No. 3 glider...

Les 5 et 6 juin 1944, nos libérateurs couraient en ces lieux sous la mitraille pour qu'aujourd'hui nous y courrions en toute liberté. 50 ans après, le 12 juin 1994, Fred Lebow, fondateur du Marathon de New-York, donnait ici le départ des Courses de la Lib

eras.summary: Location and terrain only. OpenStreetMap has no mapped outline for this site.
eras.basis: Everything drawn is traced from OpenStreetMap ways (ODbL) and the Terrarium elevation tiles. Each element names its OSM way.
eras.conjecture: Walls and buildings without a sourced height are drawn as kerb-high plan lines, never as masses. Closed walls have no gates: none are mapped. The DEM is ~30 m source resolution: it cannot show terraces, ditches or scarps. Nothing historic is depicted.
